title.rendered: I Am the Resurrection and the Life: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live.” A morning devotional for anyone facing death, loss, or the end of hope.

content.rendered:
Four days late. Her brother in the tomb. Her hope buried with him. Martha ran down the dusty road outside Bethany and met Jesus with a sentence that carried a lifetime of grief. And Jesus answered her with the sentence that would change how the church thinks about death forever.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, August 25, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Jesus said to her, ‘I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in Me, though he may die, he shall live. And whoever lives and believes in Me shall never die. Do you believe this?'”
John 11:25-26 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The word had reached Bethany four days too late. Lazarus was already in the tomb. His sisters, Mary and Martha, had watched him die, wrapped the body themselves, and walked with the mourners to the grave. Then, on the fourth day, someone came running. Jesus was on the outskirts of the village. Martha did not wait. She ran down the road to meet Him. And when she found Him, the sentence that came out of her carried a lifetime of grief compressed into one line. “Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.”

Jesus did not correct her. He did not defend His delayed arrival. He did not lecture her on divine timing. He met her exactly where she was standing, in her grief, in her disappointment, in her honest confusion, and He said something that reordered the entire universe of her thinking. “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in Me, though he may die, he shall live. And whoever lives and believes in Me shall never die.” Then He asked her the question He is still asking every believer standing at every grave. “Do you believe this?”

The Passion Translation renders it with striking depth: “Jesus said to her, ‘You don’t have to wait until then. I am the Resurrection, and I am Life Eternal. Anyone who clings to me in faith, even though he dies, will live forever'” (John 11:25 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I am [Myself] the Resurrection and the Life. Whoever believes in (adheres to, trusts in, and relies on) Me, although he may die, yet he shall live” (John 11:25 AMPC). Jesus does not merely give resurrection. He is the Resurrection. He does not merely offer life. He is the Life. To have Him is to have both.

The Greek phrase is again ego eimi. Not “I do resurrection.” Not “I give resurrection.” I am. The One standing on the dusty road outside Bethany, His feet still covered in the dust of the journey, was the Resurrection Himself in human form, telling a grieving sister that death did not have the last word over her brother, and never would again, for anyone who trusted Him. Minutes later, Jesus would call Lazarus out of the tomb and prove with His voice what He had just said with His mouth. The Resurrection is not a doctrine to comfort you at the grave. The Resurrection is a Person you can trust today.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, the question Jesus asked Martha is the question He is still asking. Do you believe this? Whatever loss you have walked through, whatever grief is still sitting in you, whatever grave you are standing beside this morning, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, the Resurrection and the Life is offering Himself to you personally. He is not offering theory. He is offering Himself. Death does not have the last word over anyone who trusts Him. Believe today. Walk in the resurrection life He purchased at the cross. It is real. It is yours. And it starts now.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus is the Resurrection and the Life. He is not a distant doctrine of comfort. He is a Person, standing on the road of my grief, telling me that death does not have the last word over what I love. I believe Him today. I trust Him with the graves I have stood beside. I trust Him with the losses I still carry. I trust Him with the future He alone holds. In Him I have resurrection life today, not just after I die, but starting now. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus is the Resurrection and the Life. Death does not have the last word over what I love. I have resurrection life in Him today, starting now. I believe.
